title: availability-hedge-and-transparent-degradation-proxy
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context and motivation: We observed intermittent regional slowdowns where a small fraction of long-running requests would inflate KV-cache pressure and cause reactive circuit flips that cascaded into noisy regional failovers. This manifested as short duration but high-impact customer-facing error spikes and increased latency p99 for tenants routed to the affected zones. The goal of this change is to introduce an availability hedge layer that provides transparent degradation at the routing edge and a small 'triage proxy' component that performs fast, local offload decisions and egress pacing so backends can shed load gracefully rather than fail hard.
Summary of changes: 1) Introduce a transparent-degradation-proxy component (edge/triage) that sits between the routing mesh and regional runtime. The proxy inspects inexpensive signals (route metadata, tenant SLO budget, request size, KV-pressure indicator) and decides per-request whether to allow, throttle, or redirect to a gentle-degrade mode. 2) Add an availability-hedge policy to the router config that coordinates with the proxy via a lightweight sidecar API. Policy supports tiered actions: allow, soft-offload (low-cost model / cached prefix response), defer (short hedged retry), and hard-deny. 3) Implement egress pacing and token-bucket smoothing for cross-region spill to prevent egress spikes when a region is healing. 4) Instrument KV cache pressure gauges and expose a new metric (region.kv_pressure_score) that feeds the decision heuristic. 5) Small runtime guard: deferred request circuit that preserves in-flight KV state for a short window to allow quick reconnection without full cache rewarm.
Checklist: - [x] Design doc updated (ENG-2042) - [x] Telemetry and dashboards added for kv_pressure_score and proxy decisions - [x] Unit tests for proxy decision logic - [x] Integration test for soft-offload path - [x] Load test run in benchmark-lab showing 3x reduction in hard errors at p99 during simulated KV pressure - [x] QA smoke pass in staging
Commits (high-level): - feat(edge): add transparent-degradation-proxy skeleton and sidecar protocol - perf(router): integrate availability-hedge policy into route evaluator - fix(runtime): defer-circuit window and KV preservation logic - feat(metrics): kv_pressure_score implementation and dashboards - test: add integration and e2e scenarios for soft-offload
Behavior and rationale: The proxy intentionally makes conservative decisions using multiple weak signals to avoid unnecessary degradation. Soft-offload returns short, cached or low-cost model responses for certain classes of requests (e.g., short completions, embeddings fallback to cached vectors) and annotates responses with X-Degrade-Reason for downstream auditing. Egress pacing avoids amplifying load during recovery by limiting the number of cross-region fallbacks per second per origin region.
Changed areas/files (high-level): - edge/proxy/degradation_proxy.go (new) - edge/proxy/sidecar_api.proto (new) - router/policy/availability_hedge.go (modified) - runtime/defer_circuit.go (modified) - runtime/kv/pressure_monitor.go (new) - telemetry/dashboards/availability-hedge.json (new) - tests/integration/soft_offload_test.go (new) - benchmark-lab/scenarios/kv_pressure_surge.yaml (new) - docs/ops/availability-hedge.md (new)
CI and validation: Initial CI run failed 1/34 integration matrix due to a flaky timing assertion in soft_offload_test. Fixed by replacing wall-clock sleeps with a deterministic fake clock in the test harness. Subsequent runs are green.
Load testing: benchmark-lab scenario kv_pressure_surge simulated sustained KV_pressure_score > 0.8 for 45s. With this change, hard error rate dropped from ~1.8% to ~0.6% and p99 latency decreased by ~18% for affected tenants.
Review conversation (selected highlights): Jonah Kim: "Overall strong approach, can we ensure the sidecar protocol is versioned for future fields? Also please add a short migration note for Dedicated customers." Author (Maya): "Added protocol versioning in sidecar_api.proto and documented migration steps under docs/ops; PTAL." Evelyn Zhao: "Concern: soft-offload may change credit accounting for token billing. Are we tracking cost delta?" Author: "Added a telemetry counter for soft_offload_hits and an analytics job to estimate unit-cost delta; included note in release notes." Carlos Mendes: "Minor: rename kv_pressure_score -> region_kv_pressure for clarity." Author: "Agree, renamed and updated dashboards."
Security and safety: The proxy performs only routing decisions and does not have access to unencrypted request bodies; decisions rely on metadata and length heuristics. Soft-offload responses are sanitized and only use cached outputs or succinct fallbacks; no fresh PII-sensitive completions are generated in degrade mode.
Rollout plan: 1) Canary deploy transparent-degradation-proxy to 5% of traffic in eu-west-1 with feature flag 'availability_hedge.v1' enabled. 2) Monitor region_kv_pressure and soft_offload_hits for 48h. 3) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% over 3 days if metrics stable.
Rollback plan: Feature flag off; routed traffic reverts to existing behavior with no stateful schema changes.
Release notes: "Introduce Availability Hedge routing and Transparent Degradation Proxy to reduce hard failures during KV pressure events. Enables soft-offload and cross-region egress pacing. Initial rollout as opt-in feature flag."
Post-merge actions: - Deploy dashboards to on-call Grafana - Run a short analytics job to baseline cost impact of soft-offload (ENG-2078) - Create follow-up task to expose per-tenant soft-offload quotas and billing labels
Related linear/JIRA: ENG-2042 design, ENG-2078 analytics follow-up. Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals from Jonah and Evelyn. Hotfix label applied and cherry-pick prepared for release/2024-11-10 branch.
